reasoning: The only posts that reached real audiences were human body and psychology reels: sleep (104), memory (94) and tickling (61). Off-niche news reached 0-5. I am staying with a body/psychology reel, but the last 4 posts were all human body, so I chose yawning. It mixes brain, body and animals and is very interactive: viewers yawn while watching, which invites comments and sends to friends. This runs version B of the hook test (a direct challenge or claim instead of a question). I am posting it as a Trial Reel because we have about 0 followers, so this costs nothing and gives the first trial-reel data. Five short slides keep the reel short. I chose documentary music (94 reach, lowest recent skip rate) and palette 2 to keep rotating.
topic: Yawning: contagion, dogs, womb, brain cooling
hook: Try not to yawn before the end

slides.title: It spreads by sight
slides.body: In Robert Provine's studies, about 55% of people yawned within 5 minutes of watching someone else yawn.
slides.image_prompt: A lion with its mouth wide open in a big yawn, golden savanna light, soft background blur
slides.credit: Kitty Terwolbeck from The Netherlands (CC BY 2.0) via wikimedia

slides.title: Reading works too
slides.body: Just reading or thinking about yawning can trigger a yawn. Feeling it yet?
slides.image_prompt: An open book resting on a soft pillow beside a cup of tea, warm lamp light, cozy sleepy mood

slides.title: Dogs catch ours
slides.body: In a 2008 study, 21 of 29 dogs yawned after watching a human yawn in front of them.
slides.image_prompt: A sleepy dog mid-yawn on a wooden floor, warm afternoon sunlight, shallow depth of field

slides.title: It starts in the womb
slides.body: Babies already yawn in the womb at about 11 weeks, but most can't catch yawns until age 4 or 5.
slides.image_prompt: A tiny knitted baby blanket and a crescent moon mobile glowing softly in a dark nursery, dreamy blue tones

slides.title: It may cool your brain
slides.body: A leading theory: a deep yawn pulls in cool air and boosts blood flow, helping chill a warm brain.
slides.image_prompt: An anatomical brain model surrounded by frost and drifting cool blue mist, dark background, cinematic light

cta: Follow for a new fact every day
caption:
Yawning is weirdly contagious. In Robert Provine's experiments, about half of people yawned within minutes of watching others yawn. For many, just reading about it is enough.

It even jumps between species. In one study, most dogs yawned after watching a person yawn. Yet babies, who already yawn in the womb, don't catch yawns until around age 4.

Be honest: how many times did you yawn while watching this? 🥱
